mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days, as reduced borrowing costs enhance corporate profitability and equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no positive correlation with FEDFUNDS levels (Rank IC < 0.03) or t-test p-value > 0.05 for the relationship over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.5% signals labor market deterioration, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5% (sign test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in payroll growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates severe labor market contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal fails when PAYEMS growth < 0 and UNRATE > 4.0% produces positive 20-day returns in >50% of cases (sign test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, declining housing starts (HOUST) signal weakening consumer demand and recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal does not hold during late-cycle expansions (GDP growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4.0%) with HOUST decline, producing positive 20-day returns in >50% of cases (sign test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.5% annualized growth for three months signals supply chain disruption and economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when INDPRO growth < -0.5% for 3 months (sign test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When annualized inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 6.0%, it triggers aggressive monetary tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 6.0% (sign test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll growth rate above 0.5% signals robust labor market conditions and rising consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% (sign test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal fails when HOUST < 0.5% growth and RSAFS < 0.3% growth produces positive 20-day returns in >50% of cases (sign test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.
